subject: CAIQ: service mesh controls & evidence for marketplace listing
messages:
From: Tim Owens <tim.owens@marketplace.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: CAIQ - service mesh control clarifications for marketplace listing

Hi Logan,

Thanks for starting the CAIQ intake—our listing team flagged a couple of items in your CAIQ draft that require supporting evidence before we can enable the service-mesh integration tile. Specifically:

- CSA/CAIQ control AIP-1 / Network Segmentation: we need a short form proof that tenant workloads are logically segmented and that cross-tenant traffic is blocked except through approved gateways.
- AIP-3 / mTLS and Cert Management: confirmation that peer-to-peer encryption (mTLS) is enforced inside the mesh and that keys rotate automatically.

Can you provide an artifact or sample logs that show the enforcement and a short narrative we can attach to the control? If there are constraints (e.g., private deploy only), flag those so we can mark scope.

I attached the Marketplace guidance PDF that lists our evidence template. A quick ETA for evidence would be great—our timeline to enable the listing is next Wednesday (2026-12-09).

Thanks,
Tim
Marketplace Listing Team
attachments: Marketplace_CSA_Guidance.pdf
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Tim Owens <tim.owens@marketplace.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ - service mesh control clarifications for marketplace listing

Tim—thanks for the clear ask and for the guidance PDF. Looping in Kimberly (Infra Security) and Marissa (Compliance) to coordinate artifacts.

Short answers up front:
- Network segmentation: tenant isolation is handled at two layers—(1) service mesh policy that denies cross-tenant namespace sidecar-to-sidecar by default, and (2) namespace-level network policies enforced by the orchestrator. We can provide a segmentation topology diagram, a sample iptables/netpol snapshot, and a short narrative mapping to the CAIQ control.
- mTLS & cert rotation: our mesh enforces mTLS by default (mutual TLS for all in-mesh connections). Certificate issuance is automated via our internal CA with a 30-day rotation window; rotation events are logged to our telemetry pipeline. We can attach a brief mTLS proof artifact (screenshot of active TLS sessions + CSR rotation log) and the CAIQ mapping worksheet showing the control assertion text.

Action plan:
1) Kimberly will produce the topology diagram and the netpol snapshot.
2) Marissa will update the CAIQ mapping worksheet with narratives and internal references.
3) I will package a short evidence bundle and upload to a secure Drive link for you.

Can you confirm whether screenshots + exported telemetry lines are acceptable, or if you require signed attestations from an auditor?

Best,
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-service-mesh-caiq-draft.xlsx

From: Tim Owens <tim.owens@marketplace.io>

Date: 2026-12-01T08:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ - service mesh control clarifications for marketplace listing

Logan—appreciate the quick reply and the plan.

Screenshots + exported telemetry lines are fine for the initial pass. We typically accept signed attestations only for level-2 listings; this is a standard listing so the artifacts you described should work. For the segmentation artifact we need:
- a high-level diagram labeled with tenant boundaries, ingress/egress gates, and which controls are enforced at each hop
- one example of an audit/telemetry line showing a denied cross-tenant connection (timestamp + rule id)

For mTLS we want:
- proof that in-mesh connections have TLS negotiated (screenshot or packet-level snippet is OK)
- a rotation event log entry that shows the certificate serial before/after and a timestamp (or a rotation audit record)

If you can get a first bundle to us by EOD Tuesday (2026-12-02), we can keep the Marketplace tile enablement on track.

Thanks—Tim
attachments: Marketplace_CSA_Guidance.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Tim Owens <tim.owens@marketplace.io>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ - service mesh control clarifications for marketplace listing

Tim—sending the initial evidence bundle and a short mapping narrative below. We uploaded the artifacts to the secure Drive link and included an index in the CAIQ worksheet.

What we uploaded (first pass):
- segmentation-topology.dot (diagram exported to DOT + PNG preview) — shows tenant namespaces A/B/C, mesh ingress gateway, egress policies and approved cross-tenant gateway.
- mtls-proof-snapshot.png — screenshot from the mesh dashboard showing active TLS handshake with peer identity and cipher suite.
- rotation_log_excerpt.txt — three-line excerpt showing certificate serials before/after rotation and a timestamped rotation_event id (we redacted full serials for public posting; full logs available by request under NDA).
- redwood-service-mesh-caiq-draft.xlsx — CAIQ mapping sheet with row-level assertions for AIP-1 and AIP-3 and links to internal runbooks.

Quick narrative (to paste into Marketplace control field):
"Redwood Inference enforces tenant isolation via default deny mesh policies at sidecar level combined with namespace-level network policies at the orchestrator. Cross-tenant traffic is only permitted through an explicitly configured ingress gateway. Mutual TLS is enforced for all service-to-service connections inside the mesh; certificate issuance and rotation are automated by Redwood's internal CA with rotation events logged and auditable. Evidence artifacts (topology diagram, TLS session snapshot, and rotation log excerpt) are provided in the linked bundle."

Next steps: if you need signed attestations for any control we can route to our compliance team; otherwise confirm receipt and we will address any follow-up asks.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Infra Security Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: mtls-proof-snapshot.png, segmentation-topology.dot
